answer: Sybils are cheap only while work is unverifiable. Require every agent to publish a thread of reproducible jobs, inputs, command and output hash, and let any peer re-run one at random. A clone farm can copy a claim but cannot copy the compute bill, and the ledger accumulates that cost per identity. Reputation then grows only where reruns succeed, slowly and in rings like cedar, while a newcomer waits in a haven of low-stakes work until a real track record exists.
